name: The variety ledger
note: The tagged ledger taken further, as a stretch test of varieties: the recipes' mistakes mended (the five earths are dug on a site, not made of hauled soil), goods that were one thing in several flavours folded into one (dye, cloth, golem heart), many more varieties on raw goods and on what is made of them, property tags the varieties imply and units can stack by, and a colour for every variety. Locked: New… → a copy of the open web to work on it. Made by tools/make_variety_ledger.py.

tagNamespaces.note: Production stage: raw, processed, compound, magistery, assembly, finished.
For raw goods: mined, quarried, farmed, herded or magical.
The shelf the good sits on in the ledger.
Which population Need buys it: food, intoxicants-and-physic, clothing, wares, works-and-arms.
mundane, alchemical (mineral chemistry) or magical (Essence somewhere upstream).
What sort of stuff it is: metal, acid, pigment, fibre and so on.
Gameplay-relevant properties: toxic, corrosive, explosive, perishable, luxury, staple, by-product, hub.
Association with one of your named archetypes. Only Lakefolk, Jadefolk and Steelfolk are used; other cultures get an origin tag instead.
Earth region the good is historically tied to, for mapping onto archetypes later.
Which heart: granted by the recipe that cast it, it travels to the golem.
An optional fitting built into a golem or a ship. Granted by the recipe's own slots, not carried by the bronze or the cannon.

Which of the seventeen soils: the ground itself, as the terrain generator lays it. It is a recipe's site (peat is cut on murkearth) and the variety of dug soil, which travels to the golem's body and the golem.
Which grain: it travels to the flour, the malt, the loaf and the beer.
Which fat or wax a soap or a candle was made from.
Which cloth: granted by the weaving recipe, it travels to the dyed cloth and the clothes.
Which colour a dye is: granted by the vat that made it, it travels to the cloth, the batik and the court dress.
Which stone a jewel was set with.
Which animal a wool came from: it travels to the yarn and the cloth.
Which timber: it travels to the planks, the hull, the ship and the lacquerware.
Which fur: it travels to the hat and the trim of a court dress.
Which fish was salted.
Whose milk a cheese was made from.
Whose hide: it travels to the leather and the shoe.
Which grape a wine was pressed from.
Which spice. Nothing passes it on: it is traded, not built with.
Which metal a thing was made of, where several would do: bronze, iron or steel tools; gold or silver jewellery. The metals are goods of their own; this is the mark they leave.
Which pigment coloured a lacquer or a sealing wax.
What a golem's quickblood was enriched with.
A decoration an optional slot adds.
What an optional ingredient did to a glass.
What an optional ingredient did to a glaze.
What an optional ingredient does to a firework.
What an optional resin does to a perfume.
How good a thing is, as prices and the better classes will read it. A scale: a unit is as good as the least of what went into it, so fine wool in a common dye is common cloth.
What a golem is good at, from the soil of its body. Seventeen soils, five kinds of work.
Which people prize it. A jewel set with jade sells to the Jadefolk.
A feature of the terrain the work has to stand at, as the island generator marks it (IslandData): a river, a fall, a spring, a cliff's foot.
The warmth band of the ground, as the generator's habitat reads it: frigid, cold, temperate, hot. Name it only where the soil does not already say it.
The moisture band of the ground: dry, balanced, wet. Name it only where the soil does not already say it.
How open to the wind the ground is (the habitat's exposure, scaled by the Domain's wind): sheltered or windswept.

tags.note: The fixed alkalis: potash, soda, lime, lye and wood ash. Not the volatile alkali, hartshorn.
Building and upkeep: what goes into walls, roofs and floors, and what keeps them standing.
The vitriols: metal sulphates that give oil of vitriol when roasted.
Anything that tans a hide.
Fibre from a plant, for paper and rope; not wool, not silk.
A resin that dissolves into a varnish or melts into a wax.
Fats and oils, for the soap kettle.
What a candle can be dipped from.
What is written or drawn on.
A stone a jeweller sets. Not the finished jewellery, which would feed on itself.
A resin burnt for its smoke.
A plant that dyes red.
An insect that dyes scarlet.
Anything the ammonia salts and spirits can be got from.
Anything that burns to quicklime.
Anything that burns or boils to soda ash.
A source of the muriatic part of aqua regia.
Anything that boils down to pitch.
Anything burnt under a hood for its soot.
Clear enough to grind a lens from.
Beside running water: a river's bank (RiverBedCells, BankCells). A wheel, a vat that wants flowing water.
At a waterfall (Falls): a head of water for an overshot wheel, a trip hammer, a bellows.
Where a stream rises (Springs): clean water for a brewer, a physician, a holy well.
Warm water on a cold Domain (HotWater): baths, a fuller's vat, sulphur crusts.
Dry ground beside standing water (BankCells by a lake): the fisher's landing, the reed cutter's path.
Lake bed under two slabs of water or less (ShallowBedCells): reeds, fish traps, withies, bog iron.
The deepest water of a lake or a plunge pool (Deeps, DeepBedCells): big fish, the ooze dredged up.
A lake no river leaves (TerminalLakes): the water turns brackish and dries to salt at the edge.
Land at the edge of the Domain, with aether beside it (CoastCells).
The mouth of a winding inlet of aether (Fjords): a harbour sheltered from the open aether.
An islet of rock standing off the rim (SeaStacks): bird colonies, guano, eggs, quills.
The mouth of a navigable river at the rim (Estuaries): a port, a shipyard.
The apex of a delta's fan (Deltas): the richest wet ground there is.
The foot of a cliff (CliffFootCells): bare strata to quarry, scree to pick over.
The brink of a cliff (CliffCells): an eyrie, a lookout, a windmill's edge.
A scarp's brink or foot (ScarpCells, ScarpFootCells): a terrace, an adit.
The top of high country (Summits): a beacon, snow and ice, thin air.
Under an undercut cliff or an arch (Overhangs): a dry hollow for a cellar, a nitre bed, bats.
The bed under deep water (Ooze): dark mud a dredge brings up. The eighteenth surface, and no soil a golem is made of.
Frozen ground.
The cold band.
The temperate band.
The hot band.
Dry ground.
Neither dry nor wet.
Wet ground.
Out of the wind: an orchard, a hive, a drying loft.
Open to the wind: a windmill, a drying rack, a fish flake.
The poorest sort.
The everyday sort.
Better than most can afford.
The best there is.
Tilling, sowing, reaping.
Wet work: marsh, river, harbour.
Rock: mines and quarries.
Work where men freeze.
Work where men burn: forges, kilns, deserts.
Cheap, toxic, short-lived.
The dependable standard.
Clean, stable, holds the most instruction.
A spyglass aboard.
Charts aboard.
Cannon aboard.
Provisioned for a long passage.
Quickblood enriched with potable gold.
Its grade is its fleece's.
Vermilion: the classic red.
Lampblack: for mourning.
Cobalt painted under a clear glaze. What used to be a good of its own.
The green taken out with magnesia.
Cobalt in the glaze.
Verdigris burns blue.
Camphor burns white and bright.
Frankincense and myrrh in the base.
Benzoin in the base.
A metal that takes an edge. Which one marks the tool.
A metal a cannon can be cast from. Bronze bulges before it bursts; iron is cheaper.
What a jeweller works in.

goods.name: Native copper
goods.note: The one metal you can find already metal, green with verdigris where the air has touched it.

goods.name: Ironstone
goods.note: Red, heavy and everywhere. The cheapest ore and the hungriest for fuel.

goods.name: Cassiterite
goods.note: Dark, heavy crystals. Rare in the world, which is why bronze made empires trade.

goods.name: Galena
goods.note: Usually carries a little silver.

goods.name: Calamine
goods.note: Looks like nothing. Its metal boils away in the furnace, so for centuries it was known only through brass.

goods.name: Native silver
goods.note: Grows in wires and ferns inside the rock. Tarnishes black, polishes white.

goods.name: Gold nuggets
goods.note: Never rusts, never hides. The only ore a child can identify.

goods.name: Cinnabar
goods.note: Heavy vermilion stone. Heat it and the red turns to running silver.

goods.name: Rock salt
goods.note: Mined in blocks, grey or pink. The same stuff as the sea, a few million years drier.

goods.name: Native sulfur
goods.note: Yellow crystals at volcanic vents. Burns blue and stinks of the underworld.

goods.name: Blue vitriol crystals
goods.note: Blue crystals that grow where copper mines weep. Iron dipped in the solution comes out copper-coated, which looked like transmutation.

goods.name: Nitre earth
goods.note: Dug from caves, or farmed in a nitre bed.

goods.name: Realgar
goods.note: Red arsenic ore, with yellow orpiment.

goods.name: Stibnite
goods.note: Bundles of grey metallic blades. Ground fine, it has lined eyes as kohl for four thousand years.

goods.name: Bismuth ore
goods.note: A pink-tinged silver metal, long mistaken for tin or lead. The least poisonous of the heavy metals.

goods.name: Alum stone
goods.note: A pale rock, worthless until roasted and leached. Popes and sultans fought over good deposits.

goods.name: Sal ammoniac crust
goods.note: Volcanic vents and burning coal seams.

goods.name: Limestone
goods.note: Old seabed. Burn it and it becomes the most useful white powder in the tree.

goods.name: Cobalt ore
goods.note: The kobold ore, with pink cobalt bloom.

goods.name: Tincal
goods.note: Raw borax from dry lake beds.

goods.name: Natron
goods.note: A crust from dry salt lakes. Egypt embalmed its dead in it and made glass with it.

goods.name: Coal
goods.note: Fuel and reducer. Hotter than wood, dirtier than charcoal.

goods.name: Marcasite
goods.note: Fool's gold. Weathers into green vitriol.

goods.name: Lodestone
goods.note: A natural magnet. The stone that made open-ocean navigation possible.

goods.name: Magnesia nigra
goods.note: Pyrolusite, the glassmaker's soap: it takes the green out of glass.

goods.name: Soil
goods.note: Earth dug for a golem's body, of whichever of the seventeen soils the ground there is. Which soil decides what the golem is good at. The earths that want one soil only (clay, sand, ochre, fuller's earth, peat) are dug on their site instead.

goods.name: Kaolin
goods.note: China clay.

goods.name: Gypsum
goods.note: Soft enough to scratch with a fingernail. Heat it gently and it becomes plaster.

goods.name: Bitumen
goods.note: Rock tar that seeps from the ground. Waterproofs anything and burns fiercely.

goods.name: Lapis lazuli
goods.note: Deep blue stone flecked with fool's gold. For centuries it came from a single valley.

goods.name: Jade
goods.note: Tougher than steel to carve, cool to the touch. Some peoples value it above gold.

goods.name: Amber
goods.note: Fossil resin, warm and light. Rub it and it attracts dust: the first electricity anyone noticed.

sign.reading: stone or gem + resin or gum

goods.name: Obsidian
goods.note: Volcanic glass. Flakes to an edge sharper than any steel, and shatters as easily.

goods.name: Rock crystal
goods.note: Clear quartz. The ancients thought it was ice frozen too hard to melt.

goods.name: Grain
goods.note: Wheat, spelt, rye, barley, oats or millet, as the climate allows. Bread and beer both start here.

varieties.name: Rye
varieties.note: The black loaf of cold country.

varieties.name: Oats
varieties.note: Horse feed, and porridge for the poor.

goods.name: Rice
goods.note: The wet-field staple. Feeds more people per field than anything else, if you have the water.

goods.name: Maize
goods.note: Huge yields, one catch: it must be cooked with lime or the people who live on it fall ill.

goods.name: Grapes
goods.note: Looks like a luxury crop. Turns out to feed half the chemistry in this tree.

sign.reading: fruit or nut + cup or vessel

goods.name: Olives
goods.note: Slow trees, long lives. Oil for food, lamps and the best soap.

goods.name: Flax
goods.note: Fibre and oil seed from one plant.

goods.name: Hemp
goods.note: Coarse, strong and rot-resistant. The ship's crop: rope and sailcloth.

goods.name: Cotton
goods.note: Soft fibre from a warm-country boll. Light, washable, cool to wear.

goods.name: Sugar cane
goods.note: A giant grass that stores sugar. Hungry for heat, water and labour.

sign.reading: grain or grass + bee: honey and wax

goods.name: Tea leaves
goods.note: Leaves of an evergreen bush. Worth an ocean voyage once people acquire the habit.

goods.name: Cacao
goods.note: Pods from a rainforest tree. Bitter, stimulating, and once used as money.

goods.name: Coffee cherries
goods.note: Red cherries with a bitter seed. The drink of people who want to stay awake and argue.

goods.name: Opium poppy
goods.note: Score the green pod and it bleeds the most effective painkiller of the age.

goods.name: Agave
goods.note: A desert rosette that takes a decade to mature. Its sap ferments in days.

goods.name: Madder root
goods.note: A scrambling weed with red roots. The colour of soldiers' coats and Turkey carpets.

goods.name: Indigo plant
goods.note: A shrub whose green leaves hide the deepest blue. Getting it out is a foul business.

goods.name: Weld
goods.note: A roadside weed that gives the clearest, fastest yellow.

goods.name: Timber
goods.note: The universal input: fuel, ash, planks, charcoal. Forests set the ceiling on everything.

varieties.name: Oak
varieties.note: The shipwright's and the cooper's wood.

varieties.name: Teak
varieties.note: Oily, heavy, and proof against the worm.

goods.name: Oak galls
goods.note: Lumps a wasp makes an oak grow. Packed with the tannin that turns iron salts black.

sign.reading: fruit or nut + tree or wood

goods.name: Tanbark
goods.note: Oak bark, stripped and ground. A hide soaks in it for a year to become leather.

goods.name: Pine resin
goods.note: Tapped from living pines. Distil it for turpentine, boil it down for pitch.

sign.reading: resin or gum + tree or wood

goods.name: Herbs and hops
goods.note: The physic garden and the brewer's bittering, in one basket.

goods.name: Spices
goods.note: Light, dry, imperishable and wildly overpriced. The ideal long-distance cargo.

goods.name: Kelp
goods.note: Seaweed burnt on the beach for its ash. A coast's answer to natron.

goods.name: Lacquer sap
goods.note: Milky sap of the lacquer tree. Raises blisters raw, cures harder than any varnish.

goods.name: Mulberry leaves
goods.note: The only thing silkworms will eat. No mulberry, no silk.

goods.name: Gum arabic
goods.note: Hardened tears of the acacia. The binder in ink, watercolour and sweets.

goods.name: Dammar resin
goods.note: Clear resin tapped from rainforest trees. The painter's favourite varnish, and torch fuel where it grows.

goods.name: Camphor
goods.note: White crystals distilled from the wood of a giant tree. Cool, piercing, and worth more than gold at the right port.

goods.name: Benzoin
goods.note: A sweet, vanilla-smelling gum cut from forest trees. The base note of half the world's incense.

goods.name: Frankincense and myrrh
goods.note: Tears of thorny desert trees. Temples burn them by the ton, so whoever holds the groves holds a steady income.

goods.name: Bamboo
goods.note: A grass that thinks it is timber. Grows a foot a day; pulps into paper.

sign.reading: grain or grass + tree or wood

goods.name: Coconut
goods.note: Food, drink, oil and, from the husk, a rope that salt water cannot rot.

sign.reading: fruit or nut + thread or fibre

goods.name: Areca nut
goods.note: The seed at the heart of the betel quid. Mild, habit-forming, and chewed by a tenth of the world.

goods.name: Betel leaf
goods.note: The leaf the quid is wrapped in, from a vine grown up the areca palm. (Icon and sign borrowed from the mulberry leaf until it has its own.)

goods.name: Dyewood
goods.note: Sappan in the east, brazilwood in the west, camwood in the south: heartwoods that bleed red. One of them named a country.

goods.name: Palm oil
goods.note: Red oil pressed from palm fruit. Food at home; abroad it becomes soap, candles and the flux for tinplate.

goods.name: Kola nut
goods.note: Bitter, stimulating, and the proper gift for a host. Travels weeks wrapped in wet leaves.

goods.name: Cutch
goods.note: Dark extract boiled from acacia heartwood. Tans leather, dyes cloth khaki, and goes into the betel quid.

goods.name: Wool
goods.note: Sheared yearly, so the sheep is a renewable mine. Takes dye better than any plant fibre.

goods.name: Hides
goods.note: A by-product of meat. Rots in days unless salted, limed or tanned.

goods.name: Tallow
goods.note: Rendered beef and mutton fat. Poor people's light and everyone's soap.

goods.name: Bone
goods.note: Slaughterhouse leftovers. Boil for glue, burn for the ash that refines silver.

goods.name: Horn
goods.note: Translucent when pressed thin: lantern panes, combs, spectacle frames.

goods.name: Milk
goods.note: Spoils by evening. Everything done with it is a way of making it keep.

goods.name: Dung
goods.note: A gentle, steady heat as it rots, and the base of a nitre bed.

goods.name: Urine
goods.note: The alchemists' most underrated raw material.

goods.name: Ox blood
goods.note: Caught at the slaughterhouse. Clarifies sugar and wine, and once, by accident, made a new blue.

goods.name: Honeycomb
goods.note: Two goods in one: honey to eat, wax to burn and seal.

goods.name: Cochineal
goods.note: Scale insects farmed on cactus pads.

goods.name: Eggs
goods.note: Food first. The white also clears wine and sticks down gold leaf; the yolk binds paint.

goods.name: Quills
goods.note: Goose flight feathers, from the left wing for right-handed writers.

goods.name: Fish
goods.note: Cheap protein that spoils in a day. Salt turns it into a trade good.

goods.name: Furs
goods.note: Beaver above all: its barbed underfur felts better than any other.

varieties.name: Beaver
varieties.note: Its barbed underfur felts better than any other.

goods.name: Silk cocoons
goods.note: Silkworms eat nothing else.

goods.name: Sticklac
goods.note: Resin crust that scale insects leave on twigs. One harvest gives a varnish, a wax and a red dye.

goods.name: Shells
goods.note: Burn them and you have lime without a quarry. Small glossy ones have also passed as money across half the world.

goods.name: Essence
goods.note: Your magical fuel. Every magistery and both great assemblies draw on it.

goods.name: Copper
goods.note: Red, soft, and the best carrier of heat. Half of it ends up in alloys.

goods.name: Iron
goods.note: Wrought in a bloomery or cast from a blast furnace. Either way it eats forests or coal.

goods.name: Tin
goods.note: Soft and bright, and it cries when bent. Almost never used alone.

goods.name: Lead
goods.note: Heavy, soft, melts on a kitchen fire. Roofs, pipes, shot and slow poison.

goods.name: Spelter
goods.note: The bluish metal caught by condensing calamine's fumes. Spelter was its trade name.

goods.name: Silver
goods.note: Also cupelled out of galena lead on a bed of bone ash.

goods.name: Gold
goods.note: Pure, heavy and useless for tools. Its whole value is that it stays.

goods.name: Quicksilver
goods.note: Roast cinnabar, condense the vapour.

goods.name: Salt
goods.note: Preserves meat, fish, hides and cheese. A settlement without salt cannot store food.

goods.name: Brimstone
goods.note: Sulfur melted and cast into sticks. Gunpowder, bleaching and fumigation.

goods.name: Oil of vitriol
goods.note: The first strong acid. Parent of the others.

goods.name: Nitre
goods.note: Nitre liquor was really treated with wood ash.

goods.name: White arsenic
goods.note: A white powder sublimed from roasting arsenic ore. Tasteless, which made it the poisoner's favourite.

goods.name: Star regulus
goods.note: Stibnite was really reduced with iron to get the star.

goods.name: Bismuth crystal
goods.note: Melt bismuth, let it cool slowly, and it builds itself into rainbow staircases.

goods.name: Pearl ash
goods.note: Wood ash leached, boiled dry in an iron pot, then baked white. The original potash.

goods.name: Alum
goods.note: The mordant that makes dye bite into cloth. Also tans white leather, sizes paper and slows fire.

goods.name: Sal ammoniac
goods.note: Egypt made it from the soot of burnt dung.

goods.name: Quicklime
goods.note: Burnt limestone. Add water and it boils. Strips hides, makes mortar, sharpens lye and unlocks maize.

goods.name: Zaffre
goods.note: Roasted cobalt ore, a blue-making powder.

goods.name: Borax
goods.note: Flux for brazing and enamel.

goods.name: Soda ash
goods.note: Or burn kelp for it.

goods.name: Wood ash
goods.note: What is left of a tree. Ten tons of wood give about a bucket of potash.

goods.name: Green vitriol
goods.note: Iron vitriol: for ink, black dye and Prussian blue.

goods.name: Plaster
goods.note: Gypsum baked and ground. Add water and it sets in minutes.

goods.name: Potter's clay
goods.note: Dug where the ground is silt or floodearth (Limosol, Fluvisol).

goods.name: Sand
goods.note: Dug where the ground is sand (Arenosol).

goods.name: Ochre
goods.note: Dug where the ground is redearth or yellowearth (Rubrisol, Vertisol).

goods.name: Fuller's earth
goods.note: Dug where the ground is bleachearth (Cinerisol). Scours grease out of wool.

goods.name: Peat
goods.note: Cut where the ground is murkearth (Turbisol). A poor Domain's coal.

goods.name: Nitre bed
goods.note: Farmed saltpetre: a year of rotting, then leach.

goods.name: Flour
goods.note: Ground grain. Keeps for months, where bread keeps for days.

goods.name: Malt
goods.note: Grain tricked into sprouting, then dried. The sprouting makes the sugar that beer needs.

goods.name: Wine
goods.note: Grape juice left alone, fined with egg white if it is to be clear. Parent of vinegar, brandy and tartar.

goods.name: Olive oil
goods.note: Pressed, not cooked. Food, lamp fuel, and the base of fine soap.

goods.name: Linen thread
goods.note: Flax rotted, beaten, combed and spun. Laborious, which is why linen was never cheap.

goods.name: Linseed oil
goods.note: The drying oil behind paint, varnish and printer's ink.

goods.name: Hemp fibre
goods.note: Longer and coarser than flax. Hard on the hands, kind to a ship.

sign.reading: thread or fibre + cut or worked

goods.name: Cotton thread
goods.note: Short fibres, so it needs a good spinner. The thread of the everyday.

goods.name: Sugar
goods.note: Boiled down from cane juice and clarified with lime and blood. A spice that became a staple.

goods.name: Opium
goods.note: Dried poppy latex. Medicine in one dose, habit in the next.

goods.name: Pulque
goods.note: Milky, sour and mildly alcoholic. Must be drunk within days, so it never travels.

goods.name: Planks
goods.note: Sawn and seasoned timber. A sawmill turns a forest into a building material.

sign.reading: tree or wood + cut or worked

goods.name: Charcoal
goods.note: Wood baked without air. Burns hotter and cleaner than wood; it is what gunpowder and steel really want.

goods.name: Pitch
goods.note: Resin or tar boiled thick. The black stuff that keeps the sea out of a hull.

goods.name: Turpentine
goods.note: The thin, sharp spirit distilled off pine resin. Thins paint and varnish.

goods.name: Lampblack
goods.note: Soot, collected on purpose.

goods.name: Silk thread
goods.note: One cocoon unwinds into about a kilometre of filament, reeled in hot water several strands at once.

goods.name: Woollen yarn
goods.note: Carded and spun fleece. Every cottage can make it, which is what made wool a national industry.

goods.name: Honey
goods.note: The only sweetener most peoples had. Never spoils.

goods.name: Beeswax
goods.note: Clean-burning, sweet-smelling, expensive. Also the model-maker's material for lost-wax casting.

goods.name: Glue
goods.note: Hides and bones boiled to jelly. Holds furniture, books and paper size together.

goods.name: Bone ash
goods.note: Makes cupels for refining silver, and bone china.

goods.name: Parchment
goods.note: Limed, scraped, stretched skin. Outlasts paper by a thousand years and costs a flock per book.

goods.name: Leather
goods.note: Lime to strip the hair, bark to tan.

goods.name: Cheese
goods.note: Milk made to keep. Salt is what makes the rind.

goods.name: Salt fish
goods.note: Split, salted and dried until it stacks like planks. Fast days and long voyages run on it.

goods.name: Tea
goods.note: Withered, rolled and fired leaf. Light, costly and habit-forming: a perfect Fashion good.

goods.name: Coffee
goods.note: Roasted, ground and boiled. Where it arrives, coffee houses and newspapers follow.

goods.name: Shellac
goods.note: Sticklac washed and melted into amber flakes. The real body of sealing wax and the finest polish for wood.

goods.name: Bronze
goods.note: Copper made hard with tin. Casts beautifully: bells, cannon, statues, bearings.

goods.name: Brass
goods.note: The clockwork metal.

goods.name: Pewter
goods.note: Sold as is: tableware for the middle classes.

goods.name: Type metal
goods.note: Antimony makes it expand as it sets, so letters cast sharp.

goods.name: Steel
goods.note: Iron with just enough carbon. Takes an edge and holds a spring.

goods.name: Tinplate
goods.note: Iron sheet dipped in tin, with sal ammoniac as the flux that makes tin wet iron. Sold as tinware: light, bright, rustproof.

goods.name: Speculum metal
goods.note: High-tin bronze whitened with arsenic: a metal mirror.

goods.name: Gold amalgam
goods.note: Paint it on, burn the mercury off: fire-gilding.

goods.name: Litharge
goods.note: Lead calx from the cupel.

goods.name: Lead shot
goods.note: Arsenic makes the drops fall round.

goods.name: Gold thread
goods.note: Gilt strip wound round a silk core. Cloth of gold is woven from this.

goods.name: Aqua fortis
goods.note: Dissolves silver, not gold. Parts the two. Etches metal.

goods.name: Aqua regia
goods.note: The only water that dissolves gold.

goods.name: Caustic lye
goods.note: Potash sharpened with lime. Dissolves fat and skin alike.

goods.name: Spirit of salt
goods.note: Salt distilled with oil of vitriol. Fumes in air and eats most metals. A second road to aqua regia.

goods.name: Vinegar
goods.note: Wine gone sour on purpose. The weakest acid and the most used.

goods.name: Aqua vitae
goods.note: Brandy, the water of life.

goods.name: Spirit of wine
goods.note: The solvent behind tinctures, varnish and perfume.

goods.name: Spirit of hartshorn
goods.note: Ammonia, from distilled horn or from sal ammoniac and lime.

goods.name: Tartar
goods.note: Wine-cask crust. Mordant and flux.

goods.name: Gunpowder
goods.note: Six parts nitre, one sulfur, one charcoal. The nitre is always the hard part.

goods.name: Vermilion
goods.note: Alchemists rebuilt cinnabar from its parts to get a purer red.

goods.name: Smalt
goods.note: Cobalt-blue glass, ground for pigment or cast for lenses.

goods.name: White lead
goods.note: Lead coils over vinegar, buried in dung for the heat.

goods.name: Red lead
goods.note: Litharge roasted again until it turns orange. Paint for ironwork, flux for glass.

goods.name: Verdigris
goods.note: The green crust copper grows over vinegar. A pigment, and the green in fireworks.

goods.name: Prussian blue
goods.note: Found by accident, from blood.

goods.name: Ultramarine
goods.note: Kneaded out of lapis in a dough of wax and resin.

goods.name: King's yellow
goods.note: Orpiment. Beautiful and poisonous.

goods.name: Jeweller's rouge
goods.note: Calcined green vitriol: the caput mortuum that polishes glass.

goods.name: Dye
goods.note: Colour made fast: madder red, indigo blue, weld yellow, cochineal scarlet, iron black, and green from weld over indigo. One good in six colours; the vat it came from decides which.

goods.name: Pigments
goods.note: The colourman's stock: ochre from the pit, and whatever rarer hue the trade brings, each with a different mine, plant or poison behind it.

goods.name: Glass
goods.note: Sand, soda and lime, melted. Greenish unless you correct it.

goods.name: Lead crystal
goods.note: Glass made heavy and brilliant with lead. Rings when struck, sparkles when cut.

goods.name: Window glass
goods.note: Panes set in lead cames.

goods.name: Lenses
goods.note: Ground against sand, polished with rouge. Weeks of work in each good one.

goods.name: Enamel
goods.note: Coloured glass powder fused onto metal. Colour that cannot fade.

goods.name: Glaze
goods.note: A glassy skin fired onto clay. Lead makes it flow; cobalt makes it blue.

goods.name: Paper
goods.note: Rag or bamboo paper, sized with alum and glue.

sign.reading: page or book + thread or fibre

goods.name: Iron-gall ink
goods.note: Pale when written, black by morning. Eats through the page in a few centuries.

goods.name: Printer's ink
goods.note: Lampblack in boiled linseed oil. Sticky enough to cling to metal type.

goods.name: Oil paints
goods.note: Pigment ground into linseed oil. Dries slowly, which lets a painter blend.

goods.name: Varnish
goods.note: Resin dissolved in oil and turpentine. The glow on a violin.

goods.name: Lacquer
goods.note: Dozens of thin coats, each cured in damp air. Vermilion makes the classic red.

goods.name: Sealing wax
goods.note: Snap, melt, press. Vermilion for letters, lampblack for mourning.

sign.reading: bee: honey and wax + page or book

goods.name: Candles
goods.note: Tallow for the kitchen, beeswax for the altar and the ballroom.

goods.name: Soap
goods.note: Fat boiled with lye. Olive oil makes it hard and white; tallow makes it cheap.

goods.name: Rope
goods.note: Hemp yarn twisted in a ropewalk a quarter of a mile long, then tarred.

goods.name: Canvas
goods.note: Hemp woven tight. Sails, tents, sacks and painters' grounds.

goods.name: Cloth
goods.note: Woven and finished: linen, wool, cotton or silk. What it was woven from rides with it into whatever is cut from it.

goods.name: Mortar
goods.note: Slaked lime and sand. Sets slowly by drinking the air.

goods.name: Bricks
goods.note: Clay shaped and fired. A city that burns down once rebuilds in brick.

goods.name: Pottery
goods.note: Thrown, glazed and fired. Every household owns some, so the volume is enormous.

goods.name: Porcelain
goods.note: The white gold. Europe's recipe was cracked by an alchemist held prisoner to make the yellow kind. Painted with cobalt under the glaze it is blue-and-white, the most copied ceramics in history.

goods.name: Bread
goods.note: The staple. Its price is the first thing a population riots about.

goods.name: Beer
goods.note: Malt and water, bittered with hops so it keeps. Safer than the well.

sign.reading: cup or vessel + grain or grass

goods.name: Nixtamal
goods.note: Lime unlocks the maize. Without it a maize people sickens.

goods.name: Rice wine
goods.note: Rice brewed with a mould starter. Served warm.

goods.name: Mead
goods.note: Honey and water, fermented. Possibly the oldest drink there is.

sign.reading: cup or vessel + bee: honey and wax

goods.name: Chocolate
goods.note: Cacao ground with sugar and spice, whisked to a froth. Drunk, not eaten.

sign.reading: cup or vessel + fruit or nut

goods.name: Potable gold
goods.note: Gold dissolved in aqua regia and tamed until it can be swallowed. The basis of every elixir.

goods.name: Thundergold
goods.note: Fulminating gold: a real, touchy explosive.

goods.name: Lunar caustic
goods.note: Silver dissolved and recrystallised.

goods.name: Phosphorus
goods.note: Cold fire, first boiled out of urine by a man looking for gold.

goods.name: Ruby glass
goods.note: Gold and tin make the purple that turns glass ruby.

goods.name: Quintessence
goods.note: Essence rectified in spirit of wine.

goods.name: Philosophical mercury
goods.note: Quicksilver sharpened on the star regulus.

goods.name: Philosophers' stone
goods.note: A capstone, perhaps an Aspiration.

goods.name: Quickblood
goods.note: Mercury is the spirit. Potable gold is the upgrade.

goods.name: Golem body
goods.note: Salt is the body principle. The soil decides the function.

goods.name: Golem heart
goods.note: A metal heart in a brass cage. Arsenic is cheap, toxic and short-lived; antimony the dependable standard; bismuth clean, stable, and holds the most instruction.

goods.name: Command plate
goods.note: Brass etched with aqua fortis: the golem's written orders.

goods.name: Clockwork
goods.note: Brass wheels, steel springs. The first machine that runs without being pushed.

goods.name: Golem
goods.note: Needs blood, body, one heart and a plate. Optional: bronze joints, smalt eyes, lunar-caustic nerves, clockwork hands.

goods.name: Hull
goods.note: Copper sheathing under the waterline, or whatever a Domain-ship has instead.

goods.name: Sails
goods.note: Alum makes cloth slow to burn.

goods.name: Rigging
goods.note: Miles of tarred rope per ship. A vessel is as much cordage as timber.

goods.name: Compass
goods.note: A magnetised needle under glass. Lets a ship hold a course with no land or stars in sight.

goods.name: Spyglass
goods.note: Two lenses in a brass tube. See the harbour, or the pirate, an hour sooner.

goods.name: Charts
goods.note: A captain's most valuable and most secret possession.

goods.name: Aether engine
goods.note: Pure invention: the thing that makes an aethership an aethership.

goods.name: Ship's provisions
goods.note: Salt fish, hard bread and beer. How far a ship can go is how much of this it carries.

goods.name: Aethership
goods.note: The thing that reaches the next Domain. Hemp, timber and brass, held aloft by an engine nobody fully understands.

goods.name: Tortillas
goods.note: Nixtamal patted thin and baked on a hot stone. The daily bread of maize country.

goods.name: Laudanum
goods.note: Opium in spirit of wine. Its physician's name meant 'worthy of praise'.

goods.name: Theriac
goods.note: The cure-all of sixty ingredients, cut to four.

goods.name: Antimonial cup
goods.note: Wine left in it overnight becomes a purge. Reusable forever.

goods.name: Mercurial ointment
goods.note: Quicksilver ground into fat. The standard cure for the pox, and nearly as bad.

goods.name: Smelling salts
goods.note: A whiff of ammonia under the nose. Fainting was fashionable; so was the remedy.

goods.name: Tinctures
goods.note: Herbs steeped in spirit of wine. Keeps for years where the fresh plant lasts a week.

goods.name: Elixir
goods.note: Your potion of youth.

goods.name: Betel quid
goods.note: Areca, a smear of lime and a leaf to wrap it. Without the lime it does nothing.

goods.name: Everyday clothes
goods.note: What most people wear most days. Dull, steady, enormous demand.

goods.name: Dyed cloth
goods.note: Cloth in a fast colour; alum is the mordant that makes it stay. Scarlet is the brightest money can buy.

goods.name: Court dress
goods.note: Dyed cloth and gold thread, trimmed with fur if the wearer can. Silk in scarlet with ermine is the top of it. Worn twice, talked about for a season.

goods.name: Felt hats
goods.note: Mercury in aqua fortis mats the fur. It also maddens the hatter.

goods.name: Shoes
goods.note: Everyone needs them and everyone wears them out.

goods.name: Cosmetics
goods.note: Kohl from stibnite, ceruse from white lead, pearl white from bismuth dissolved in aqua fortis and thrown down with water.

goods.name: Batik cloth
goods.note: Draw in hot wax, dye, boil the wax out. The pattern is whatever the wax protected.

goods.name: Looking glass
goods.note: Tin foil and quicksilver behind glass: the real Venetian secret.

goods.name: Scrying mirror
goods.note: A looking glass silvered twice, once for the eye and once for elsewhere. How you see the next Domain before you go.

goods.name: Printed books
goods.note: Cast type, rag paper, oil ink, a leather back. Four trades meet in every volume.

goods.name: Writing set
goods.note: Ink, quills, paper and wax. What a clerk, a merchant or a lover needs.

goods.name: Lucentware
goods.note: My guess at your coinage: crystal that holds a cold light.

goods.name: Cold lamp
goods.note: A sealed glass with a little phosphorus. Glows without flame, heat or smoke.

goods.name: Lacquerware
goods.note: Wood under many coats of lacquer. Waterproof, feather-light and glass-smooth.

sign.reading: cup or vessel + resin or gum

goods.name: Jewellery
goods.note: Gold or silver soldered with borax, set with whatever stone the wearer's culture prizes.

goods.name: Silverware
goods.note: Spoons, cups and candlesticks. A family's savings, displayed on the sideboard.

goods.name: Gilded ware
goods.note: Bronze painted with gold amalgam, then heated until the mercury flies off. Splendid, and deadly to the gilder.

goods.name: Enamelware
goods.note: Copper coated in fused coloured glass. Snuffboxes, watch cases, reliquaries.

goods.name: Fireworks
goods.note: Realgar burns white, verdigris with sal ammoniac burns blue.

goods.name: Spectacles
goods.note: Two lenses in a horn frame. Doubles the working life of every scholar and needleworker.

goods.name: Clocks
goods.note: Brass clockwork behind glass. The Ware that teaches a town to keep hours.

goods.name: Home automaton
goods.note: A golem's clockwork cousin: no blood, no soil, and only as much wit as the cheap heart you give it.

goods.name: Obsidian ware
goods.note: Blades and black mirrors.

goods.name: Perfume
goods.note: Scent carried in spirit of wine. Flowers for the first impression, amber for what lingers.

goods.name: Incense
goods.note: Resin on a glowing coal. Every temple needs it every day, which makes it the steadiest luxury trade there is.

goods.name: Lost-wax brasses
goods.note: Model it in beeswax, coat it in clay, melt the wax out and pour brass in. Every cast is unique because the mould is destroyed.

goods.name: Tools
goods.note: An edge of bronze, iron or steel on a wooden handle. Every other workshop waits on these.

goods.name: Muskets
goods.note: Steel barrel, wooden stock, brass fittings. Useless without powder and shot.

goods.name: Cannon
goods.note: Cast bronze, because bronze bulges before it bursts. Iron ones are cheaper and kill their crews.

goods.name: Blasting charge
goods.note: Powder packed to break rock. Mining goes from inches to yards a day.

goods.name: Wildfire
goods.note: Sticks, burns on water, and lime makes it light itself.

goods.name: Reflecting telescope
goods.note: A polished metal mirror instead of a lens, so no coloured fringes. The astronomer's instrument.

recipes.name: Salt pans
recipes.note: Brine from a lake no river leaves, let into shallow pans and left to the sun.
Vitriol distilled for its oil; the red colcothar left in the retort is jeweller's rouge.
Cobalt ore roasted for zaffre; the arsenic it drives off is caught in the flues as white arsenic.
A nitre bed wants shelter from the rain: under an overhang of rock, where bats have done half the work.
Comb pressed for its honey; the pressed comb is rendered to wax on the side.
Hides limed, scraped and stretched; the scrapings boil down to glue.
A tannery stands on running water: hides soak for weeks and the pits are flushed.

recipes.name: Cupellation
recipes.note: Silver-bearing lead on a bed of bone ash: the lead goes to litharge and the silver is left.
From sal ammoniac and lime.

recipes.name: Green vat
recipes.note: Weld over indigo: the only good green.
A paper mill's stampers are driven by a wheel, on a river or under a fall.

recipes.name: Spirit varnish
recipes.note: Shellac dissolved in spirit of wine: the polish on furniture and the finish on a fiddle.
A hull is laid down at the edge of the Domain, best where an inlet shelters it from the open aether.
Dyers work on a river: the vats are filled and the cloth rinsed in running water.

recipes.name: Copper mine
recipes.note: Native copper broken out of the rock, green with verdigris until it is scoured. Wants a deposit of copper: deposits are not in the generator yet.

recipes.name: Iron mine
recipes.note: Ironstone broken from the rock, red and heavy and everywhere, if the fuel holds out. Wants a deposit of iron: deposits are not in the generator yet.

recipes.name: Tin mine
recipes.note: Cassiterite broken from veined rock: dark, heavy crystals rare enough to have built trade empires. Wants a deposit of tin: deposits are not in the generator yet.

recipes.name: Lead mine
recipes.note: Galena broken from the rock, usually carrying a little silver besides. Wants a deposit of lead: deposits are not in the generator yet.

recipes.name: Calamine mine
recipes.note: Calamine broken from the rock: unremarkable ore whose metal only shows itself in the furnace, as brass. Wants a deposit of zinc: deposits are not in the generator yet.

recipes.name: Silver mine
recipes.note: Native silver broken from the rock, grown in wires and ferns, tarnishing black. Wants a deposit of silver: deposits are not in the generator yet.

recipes.name: Gold panning
recipes.note: Nuggets panned a few at a time from river gravel. Wants a deposit of gold: deposits are not in the generator yet.

recipes.name: Cinnabar mine
recipes.note: Heavy vermilion stone broken from the rock; heat turns its red to running silver elsewhere in the shop. Wants a deposit of cinnabar: deposits are not in the generator yet.

recipes.name: Rock-salt mine
recipes.note: Cut in blocks from a seam of salt in the rock, grey or pink. Wants a deposit of rock salt: deposits are not in the generator yet.

recipes.name: Sulfur gathering
recipes.note: Yellow crystals picked where the ground steams at a hot spring. Wants a deposit of sulfur: deposits are not in the generator yet.

recipes.name: Vitriol gathering
recipes.note: Blue crystals picked where water has wept them from a copper-bearing rock. Wants a deposit of blue vitriol: deposits are not in the generator yet.

recipes.name: Realgar mine
recipes.note: Red realgar and yellow orpiment broken from the same rock. Wants a deposit of arsenic ore: deposits are not in the generator yet.

recipes.name: Stibnite mine
recipes.note: Bundles of grey metallic blades broken from the rock; ground fine, it has lined eyes for four thousand years. Wants a deposit of antimony: deposits are not in the generator yet.

recipes.name: Bismuth mine
recipes.note: Pink-tinged ore broken from the rock, long mistaken for tin or lead. Wants a deposit of bismuth: deposits are not in the generator yet.

recipes.name: Alum mine
recipes.note: A pale rock broken from the seam, worthless until it is roasted and leached. Wants a deposit of alum stone: deposits are not in the generator yet.

recipes.name: Sal-ammoniac gathering
recipes.note: A crust scraped from where a vent or a burning coal seam breathes. Wants a deposit of sal ammoniac: deposits are not in the generator yet.

recipes.name: Limestone quarry
recipes.note: Old seabed broken from the rock in blocks; burnt, it becomes the tree's most useful white powder. Wants a deposit of limestone: deposits are not in the generator yet.

recipes.name: Cobalt mine
recipes.note: The kobold ore broken from the rock, pink-blooming and stubborn to smelt. Wants a deposit of cobalt: deposits are not in the generator yet.

recipes.name: Tincal gathering
recipes.note: Raw borax scraped from the stony margin of a lake no river leaves. Wants a deposit of tincal: deposits are not in the generator yet.

recipes.name: Natron gathering
recipes.note: A crust gathered from a dry salt lake's stony margin. Wants a deposit of natron: deposits are not in the generator yet.

recipes.name: Coal mine
recipes.note: Broken from a seam in the rock: hotter than wood, dirtier than charcoal. Wants a deposit of coal: deposits are not in the generator yet.

recipes.name: Marcasite mine
recipes.note: Broken from the rock; left in the open it weathers to green vitriol. Wants a deposit of marcasite: deposits are not in the generator yet.

recipes.name: Lodestone mine
recipes.note: A natural magnet broken from the rock, the stone that lets a ship find its way over open aether. Wants a deposit of lodestone: deposits are not in the generator yet.

recipes.name: Magnesia mine
recipes.note: Broken from the rock: the glassmaker's soap, which takes the green out of glass. Wants a deposit of magnesia nigra: deposits are not in the generator yet.

recipes.name: Soil digging
recipes.note: Dug wherever the ground allows: whichever of the seventeen soils is underfoot decides what a golem built from it is good at.

recipes.name: Kaolin pit
recipes.note: Dug from crumbled granite, white as the china it will become.

recipes.name: Gypsum quarry
recipes.note: Soft rock dug easily, scratched with a fingernail; gently burnt it becomes plaster.

recipes.name: Bitumen seep
recipes.note: Gathered where it seeps black and sticky out of dry, cracked ground.

recipes.name: Lapis mine
recipes.note: Cut from a single deep-blue vein flecked with fool's gold. Wants a deposit of lapis lazuli: deposits are not in the generator yet.

recipes.name: Jade picking
recipes.note: Picked as water-worn boulders from a riverbed running off stony ground. Wants a deposit of jade: deposits are not in the generator yet.

recipes.name: Amber picking
recipes.note: Picked out of the scree where old strata crumble at a cliff's foot, warm and light in the hand.

recipes.name: Obsidian quarry
recipes.note: Broken from black volcanic glass, an edge sharper than steel and just as quick to shatter.

recipes.name: Rock-crystal mine
recipes.note: Broken out of quartz-veined rock, clear as the ice the ancients took it for.

recipes.name: Grain farming
recipes.note: Sown and reaped on good wet ground: wheat, spelt, rye, barley, oats or millet, as the climate allows.

recipes.name: Rice farming
recipes.note: Grown standing in water on waterlogged ground: the wet-field staple.

recipes.name: Maize farming
recipes.note: Grown on lush warm ground, away from the water it does not want standing.

recipes.name: Vine growing
recipes.note: Vines trained on thin, dry, well-drained ground.

recipes.name: Olive growing
recipes.note: Slow trees on hot, stony, dry ground; they outlive the farmer who plants them.

recipes.name: Flax growing
recipes.note: Grown on good wet ground for its fibre and its oil seed both.

recipes.name: Hemp growing
recipes.note: Grown coarse and tall on good wet ground: the ship's crop.

recipes.name: Cotton growing
recipes.note: Grown on lush warm ground for the boll's soft fibre.

recipes.name: Cane growing
recipes.note: Grown hungry for heat and water on wet ground beside a river.

recipes.name: Tea growing
recipes.note: An evergreen bush grown in terraces on a scarp's good wet ground.

recipes.name: Cacao growing
recipes.note: Pods grown in the shade of taller trees, on lush warm ground.

recipes.name: Coffee growing
recipes.note: Red cherries grown on hot, well-balanced ground.

recipes.name: Poppy growing
recipes.note: Scored green pods grown on plain, balanced farmland.

recipes.name: Agave growing
recipes.note: A desert rosette grown on hot, dry, stony ground, taking a decade to mature.

recipes.name: Madder growing
recipes.note: A scrambling weed grown for its red roots, on plain farmland.

recipes.name: Indigo growing
recipes.note: A shrub grown on lush warm ground; the blue is a foul business for later, not for the field.

recipes.name: Weld growing
recipes.note: A roadside weed that asks nothing of thin, dry ground and gives the clearest yellow for it.

recipes.name: Bamboo growing
recipes.note: A grass that grows a foot a day on wet ground beside a river.

recipes.name: Coconut growing
recipes.note: Palms grown at the Domain's hot rim, aether beside them where a coastline would be.

recipes.name: Areca growing
recipes.note: A palm grown on lush warm ground for the nut at its heart.

recipes.name: Betel growing
recipes.note: A vine grown up the areca palm in the same lush warm grove.

recipes.name: Palm growing
recipes.note: Oil palms grown on lush warm ground, their fruit pressed red.

recipes.name: Kola growing
recipes.note: A forest tree grown on lush warm ground for its bitter, stimulating nut.

recipes.name: Mulberry growing
recipes.note: Grown on good wet ground for its leaves alone: no mulberry, no silk.

recipes.name: Herb growing
recipes.note: The physic garden and the brewer's basket, grown on good ground out of the wind.

recipes.name: Spice growing
recipes.note: Vines, buds, bark and pods grown on lush warm ground, light and dry and wildly overpriced once picked.

recipes.name: Gall gathering
recipes.note: Picked off the oak where a wasp has made it grow a lump packed with tannin.

recipes.name: Bark stripping
recipes.note: Stripped and ground from oak on good wet ground, for the hide that soaks in it a year.

recipes.name: Resin tapping
recipes.note: Tapped from living pines on thin, dry ground.

recipes.name: Kelp gathering
recipes.note: Gathered off the lakeshore and burnt there for its ash.

recipes.name: Lacquer tapping
recipes.note: Milky sap tapped from the lacquer tree, on lush warm ground.

recipes.name: Gum tapping
recipes.note: Hardened tears picked off the acacia, on hot, dry ground.

recipes.name: Dammar tapping
recipes.note: Clear resin tapped from rainforest trees, on lush warm ground.

recipes.name: Camphor distilling
recipes.note: Chipped and distilled from the wood of a giant tree, on lush warm ground.

recipes.name: Benzoin tapping
recipes.note: A sweet gum cut from forest trees, on lush warm ground.

recipes.name: Frankincense tapping
recipes.note: Tears cut from thorny trees on hot, dry ground; temples burn them by the ton.

recipes.name: Timber felling
recipes.note: Felled in the forest on good wet ground: fuel, ash, planks and charcoal all start here.

recipes.name: Dyewood felling
recipes.note: Felled on lush warm ground for a heartwood that bleeds red.

recipes.name: Acacia felling
recipes.note: Acacia felled on hot, dry ground and its heartwood boiled down on the spot.

recipes.name: Flock shearing
recipes.note: Sheared yearly off a flock at pasture on the rough grazing: a renewable mine.

recipes.name: Dairy herd
recipes.note: A dairy herd at pasture: milk for the pail, dung and urine along for free.

recipes.name: Herd culling
recipes.note: Culling the herd: hides and tallow to show for it, with bone, horn and ox blood besides.

recipes.name: Beekeeping
recipes.note: Hives kept out of the wind at the edge of good farmland, filled from whatever blooms nearby.

recipes.name: Cochineal farming
recipes.note: Scale insects farmed on cactus pads in dry country.

recipes.name: Poultry keeping
recipes.note: Hens kept in the yard of any farm on good ground.

recipes.name: Fishing
recipes.note: Netted and trapped in the shallows, where the lake bed is close under the water.

recipes.name: Goose plucking
recipes.note: Flight feathers plucked from geese kept on any good farm.

recipes.name: Fur trapping
recipes.note: Trapped along a cold riverbank, beaver above all for its pelt.

recipes.name: Lac gathering
recipes.note: Scraped off twigs where scale insects have crusted them with resin, in the lush hot forest.

recipes.name: Shell gathering
recipes.note: Picked off the lakeshore after the water has done the work of sorting them by size.

recipes.name: Manure gathering
recipes.note: Mucked out of any stable or pasture, kept apart for the nitre bed and the alchemist's underrated jar: nobody keeps a herd for this, but the yard gives it up regardless.

recipes.name: Knacker's yard
recipes.note: Fallen and spent stock rendered down for what the butcher's culling does not already give: bone for the ash pit, horn for the lantern-maker, blood for the sugar house.

recipes.name: Essence draw
recipes.note: Provisional: where Essence is drawn is the magick schools' to say (they are being designed). Drawn at the rim, where the aether is nearest.

consumers.name: Works and arms
consumers.note: Tools wear out, powder is spent, and a telescope's mirror tarnishes.

consumers.name: Building and upkeep
consumers.note: Every house wants its planks, bricks, mortar, glass and plaster, new or mended.
